subject: Hosted API tier orchestration, monthly commit uplift & invoice cadence
messages:
From: Alex Murphy <alex@opticlane.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: move to Tier 3 + monthly commit increase

Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick usage forecast and expect Q4 to exceed our current hosted commit by ~2.6x because of a product launch. We'd like to propose moving from your Standard tier to Tier 3 (reserved monthly commit 12M tokens) starting Oct 1, with a temporary soft-burst cushion for November.

Key asks:
- Confirm rate per 1k tokens at Tier 3 and soft-burst overage policy.
- Can you align invoicing to calendar months (invoice 1st of each month) and provide a prorated first invoice for Oct 1 start?
- Need an execution-ready MAA + SOW to share with our legal/finance team.

Attaching high-level volume projection. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Alex
Alex Murphy
Head of Platform
OpticLane
attachments: OpticLane forecast Q4.csv (attachment stub)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Alex Murphy <alex@opticlane.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: move to Tier 3 + monthly commit increase

Alex—

Really appreciate the heads up and congrats on the launch. Quick answers up front:
- Tier 3 per-1k-token rate: $12.50 (net, after volume discount); soft-burst: permitted up to 25% monthly overage billed at 0.75x baseline rate for the burst window.
- We can invoice on the 1st. For an Oct 1 start we'll issue a prorated invoice for the remaining days in Oct and full monthly invoices thereafter.
- I'll send a draft MAA + SOW by end of day — looping in Karthik for pricing confirmation and Marissa for commercial signoff.

Would you like the MAA to include a 90-day performance review clause for throughput and latency SLOs? Many customers prefer a run-in period.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Alex Murphy <alex@opticlane.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: move to Tier 3 + monthly commit increase

Thanks — 90-day review clause sounds good. Finance will want clear invoice cadence and a single POC for billing disputes. Please include a single billing contact: payables@opticlane.com.

Also: can the soft-burst be split across two monthly windows instead of a single month spike? We prefer smoothing across months if possible.

—Alex

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: move to Tier 3 + monthly commit increase — pricing / terms check

Folks — forwarding the OpticLane ask. Short list of considerations:
- They want 12M monthly tokens (Tier 3) starting Oct 1, plus a 25% soft-burst that they'd prefer to split across Nov/Dec (smoothing).
- Requested invoicing on the 1st, prorated Oct invoice, payables contact is payables@opticlane.com.
- Include 90-day performance review clause.

Questions: can we accept smoothing of soft-burst across two months instead of one? If we do, what is the billing treatment and how to reflect in the MAA? Also any commercial levers we want to add (quarterly invoice discount, initial onboarding credit)?

Thanks — Tessa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: move to Tier 3 + monthly commit increase — pricing / terms check

Tessa / Marissa —

We can accommodate smoothing the soft-burst across two consecutive months, but need clarity in the MAA on how the smoothing window is calculated and how it interacts with autoscaling and overage billing. Proposed language:
- Soft-Burst Smoothing: up to 25% of monthly commit may be applied across the following two calendar months; overage billed at 0.75x baseline.
- Invoices will reflect baseline committed tokens + pro rata share of burst usage in the month it is consumed; a smoothing reconciliation line item will appear on the second month if the burst was allocated across months.

Commercial levers: offer a 2% billing discount if OpticLane elects quarterly invoicing (prepay) — helps our cash flow and reduces monthly billing friction. Also recommend a one-time onboarding credit of $6k to cover initial integration and runbook ops; present that as a limited-time concession.

Marissa — need approval on discount + credit.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales — Hosted
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Alex Murphy <alex@opticlane.com>
Cc: payables@opticlane.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API tier orchestration, monthly commit uplift & invoice cadence — final

Alex / OpticLane team —

Thanks for your patience. We reviewed internally and are prepared to move forward with the following binding terms effective Oct 1, 2026:

Summary of agreed terms:
- Committed monthly tokens: 12,000,000 (Tier 3)
- Soft-burst: up to 25% of committed tokens; smoothing allowed across two consecutive months; overage billed at 0.75x baseline rate and reconciled on the second month line item.
- Per-1k-token rate (Tier 3, net): $12.50
- Invoicing cadence: monthly on the 1st; prorated invoice for Oct (covering Oct 1–31) will be issued on Nov 1 to allow ops reconciliation; Payables POC: payables@opticlane.com
- 90-day performance review clause included in MAA (throughput and 99th percentile latency targets).
- Commercial concessions: 2% discount if OpticLane chooses quarterly prepay within 30 days of contract signature; one-time onboarding credit of $6,000 applied to the first invoice upon signature.

Attached: execution-ready MAA_v3.pdf and SOW_OpticLane_2026.docx (redlines accepted). Please confirm counterparty signing instructions and whether your legal team requires any additional exhibits.

Next steps:
1) Alex to confirm signing POC and whether OpticLane will prepay quarterly (to trigger 2% discount).
2) We will queue provisioning and capacity reservations for Oct 1 once DocuSign signature is returned.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
